description: Securing decorative and protective metalwork to a cover. Corners, shoes, and plaques are nailed to wooden boards over a leather back; Cockerell judges bindings whose metal is confined to the boards as the most successful, and prefers metal settings shown openly rather than jewels hidden beneath the leather.
name: mounting metal furniture

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (1901), Chapter XVIII, p.259. Internet Archive.
